mcq.q: Kavya starts facing East and walks 8 km. She turns left and walks 5 km. She turns left and walks 9 km. She turns right and walks 4 km. She turns right and walks 13 km. What is the straight-line distance between Kavya and the starting point?
mcq.explain: Track the net movement: the East–West total is 12 km East and the North–South total is 9 km North. These are at right angles, so the shortest distance is √(12² + 9²) = √225 = 15 km (Pythagoras). Adding the two (21 km) gives the walking path, not the straight-line distance.
mcq.fast: Net East–West and net North–South, then Pythagoras (look for 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 6-8-10 triples).

mcq.q: Meena starts facing East and walks 7 km. She turns right and walks 5 km. She turns right and walks 13 km. Where is Meena now with respect to the starting point?
mcq.explain: Net displacement: 6 km West and 5 km South. So Meena is South-West of the start. The direction Meena is FACING at the end (West) is a different question — position is about where the person is, not where they look.
mcq.topic: Final facing vs position from the start
mcq.fast: Keep running totals of East–West and North–South; their signs give the direction.

mcq.q: Kavya is facing West. Kavya turns 270° clockwise, then turns left, then turns right, then turns right. Which direction is Kavya facing now?
mcq.explain: Measure every turn in 45° steps clockwise from West: right = +90°, left = −90°, about-turn = 180°, clockwise adds and anticlockwise subtracts. The net turn is 0° clockwise, so Kavya faces West. Distances walked do not change the facing direction.
mcq.topic: Turns: left, right, angles and about-turn
mcq.fast: Add up all turns as signed degrees (clockwise +), reduce modulo 360°, then rotate the starting direction.

mcq.q: One evening, Imran stands in the sun so that Imran's shadow falls exactly to the left of Imran. Which direction is Imran facing?
mcq.explain: In the evening the sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East. The shadow is to the left of Imran, i.e. East is on the left. That happens when Imran faces South.
mcq.fast: Morning shadow points West, evening shadow points East; then turn yourself until that direction is on the stated side.

mcq.q: If North-West is called North, West is called North-West, and the other directions are renamed in the same way, what is South-West called?
mcq.explain: North-West → North is a rotation of 45° clockwise, and West → North-West confirms it. Rotating South-West by the same 45° clockwise gives West. Rotating the other way (anticlockwise) is the common mistake. Drawing the compass and turning it helps.
mcq.fast: Find the rotation angle from one given pair, then rotate the asked direction by the same angle.

mcq.q: If North-East is called South, South-East is called West, and the other directions are renamed in the same way, what is North called?
mcq.explain: North-East → South is a rotation of 135° clockwise, and South-East → West confirms it. Rotating North by the same 135° clockwise gives South-East. Rotating the other way (anticlockwise) is the common mistake. Drawing the compass and turning it helps.
mcq.fast: Find the rotation angle from one given pair, then rotate the asked direction by the same angle.

mcq.q: If West is called North, South-East is called South-West, and the other directions are renamed in the same way, what is North-West called?
mcq.explain: West → North is a rotation of 90° clockwise, and South-East → South-West confirms it. Rotating North-West by the same 90° clockwise gives North-East. Rotating the other way (anticlockwise) is the common mistake. Drawing the compass and turning it helps.
mcq.fast: Find the rotation angle from one given pair, then rotate the asked direction by the same angle.

mcq.q: P is 3 m to the South of R. T is 4 m to the West of R. In which direction is T from P?
mcq.explain: Put R at the origin: P is at (0, -3) and T at (-4, 0). Going from P to T means moving 4 m West and 3 m North, so T is North-West of P. "P from T" would be the opposite direction.
mcq.fast: Draw B as the centre, mark A and C, and read the direction from A (the reference point) to C.
